newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson helps Swedish shares to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson helps Swedish shares to end higher.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Monday, lifted by an upturn in telecoms group Ericsson and favourable European trends.
The Stockholm bourse's general index rose 1.19 percent to 2,829.69 with turnover a modest 3.49 billion crowns as trade remained subdued throughout the day.

Uncertainty about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) after the left-wing French election win and caution ahead of the Swedish government's Tuesday EMU announcement kept many investors in the sidelines, dealers said.
Ericsson led the rise, jumping six crowns to 278.
The share benefitted from positive international trends for technology shares and the group's new Internet focus, dealers said, but they did not want to read too much into the advance.
"There was not much trade at these high levels and nothing of great importance has happened," a trader said. "Ericsson can move like this in thin trade."
The drugs sector was the day's winner, up 2.69 percent, as Pharmacia & Upjohn jumped 11 crowns to 274 and Astra gained 3.5 crowns to 128.5.
"A positive article in Barron's is said to have pulled the share (Pharmacia & Upjohn) higher," a trader said.
Forestry shares and engineering shares were also strong with the forestry sector rising 1.18 percent. Engineer Atlas Copco advanced 1.5 crowns to 206.
Strong new car registrations, up 24.8 percent in May from a year earlier, lifted Volvo by 1.5 crowns to 216.
S-E-Banken rose one crown to 81 while Nordbanken ended flat at 240.

A weekend newspaper report, denied by Nordbanken, said the two were close to a deal in which Nordbanken would become a retail bank and sell its international and mutual fund operations to S-E-Banken, which would focus on merchant banking.
